title: Batching + KV-cache aliasing causing silent accuracy drift: mitigation, canary expansion, and rollout plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a production capacity scale event on 2026-02-09 we observed a gradual accuracy drift for a small set of quantized 8-bit model variants serving chat completions. The drift manifested as higher semantic hallucination rates and several customer-reported classification errors. The incident did not cause service-wide crash loops but produced correlated degraded outputs for multi-tenant workloads that used continuous batching.

What happened: Autoscaling and burst batching combined with the runtime's KV-cache prefetch path allowed requests from different model variants (same architecture but different quantization profiles) to reuse prefetched KV entries under certain race conditions. This KV aliasing resulted in silent state leakage across requests, biasing attention for subsequent tokens and producing subtle-but-measurable output drift. The bug is deterministic under a specific composition of: batched requests >2 tenants, mix of model variants (int8 + int4 candidate), and aggressive prefetch enabled by the batching heuristic.

Detection: The degradation was first flagged by a customer alert (classification regression) at 2026-02-09 22:13 UTC and confirmed by increased A/B eval failures on the quality-monitoring dashboard (alert: QUALITY_REGRESSION_QUANT_BATCHING). Canary coverage was limited to single-tenant scenarios and did not exercise mixed-variant batching, so the canary pass was green.

Impact: Affected a narrow subset (~1.6% of overall requests) but disproportionately affected workloads that rely on precise token-level logits (few-shot classification, reranking). No PII exposure or data leak. No persistent corruption of model artifacts; issue was runtime-state only.

Root cause (short): KV-cache prefetch logic reuses the same backing buffer for prefetched key/value blobs and does not fully isolate cache entries by model-variant fingerprint. Under concurrent batching, the buffer can be populated for request A then observed by request B before B applies its own quant-decompress path, leading to a mismatch between quant-format metadata and buffer contents. This mismatch does not always throw an op-fallback; it can silently produce incorrect dequantization and attention key/values that bias generation.

Engineering diagnosis links: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/QUANT-BATCH-KV-INVESTIGATION, https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ops/quality-regression-quant-batching?orgId=1
steps_taken: Immediate mitigations (2026-02-09 to 2026-02-10): throttled burst batching for mixed-model queues, disabled KV-prefetch for quantized variants, and temporarily pinned affected customer tenants to float32 variants.
Hotfix (2026-02-11): landed runtime patch that adds a per-request model-variant fingerprint into the KV-cache entry header and enforces a strict compare before reuse (PR ENG-57319/1).

Rollback/Canary: rolled patch to a subset of capacity nodes and validated end-to-end evals on our synthetic prompt set and the customer's failing prompt set. No regression observed after patch on canary nodes.

Post-incident load test (2026-02-18): ran stress tests with mixed batching patterns (2-16 requests per batch, random model-variant mixes) and verified no aliasing reproductions under 48h of continuous load.
Customer remediation: outreach to affected customers with explanation, mitigation steps, and offer to rerun failing jobs on pinned float variants while we monitor for latent issues.
action_items: Add deterministic op/fingerprint observation to request logs (short-term): per-token header that records whether request hit quantized/dequantized path (owner: Marcus Lin, due: 2026-03-05).

Expand canary matrices (medium-term): add mixed-model-variant batching scenarios to canary suite and include a small multi-tenant traffic replay for 24h before full rollout (owner: Sofia Nguyen, PM; due: 2026-03-12).
Formalize KV-cache entry schema (short-term): move to immutable cached blobs or copy-on-write semantics for prefetched KVs to eliminate aliasing (owner: Runtime infra team; due: 2026-03-22).

Quant path unit/integration tests (short-term): add fuzzing harnesses that exercise batch composition, prefetch, and concurrent flush to CI with coverage targets (owner: Diego Ruiz, SRE; due: 2026-03-08).

Autotuner safety gate (long-term): integrate quant-autotuner to flag mixed-variant unsafe batch configurations and prevent combinatorial scheduling until compatibility verified (owner: Optimize team; due: 2026-04-15).
Observability dashboards (short-term): new histogram and alert on per-request "kv-fingerprint-mismatch" and op-fallback rates by model-variant and tenant (owner: Observability team; due: 2026-03-01).
Customer canary program (ongoing): invite top affected customers to an extended canary with explicit transparency about routing and fallback thresholds (owner: Customer Success; due: 2026-03-31).
comments: 2026-02-10 Marcus Lin: Initial triage complete. Hotfix landed to enforce fingerprint compare. Deploying to canary nodes now. Need to coordinate obs changes for kv-fingerprint-mismatch.
2026-02-12 Aisha Patel: Canary evals look clean across synthetic suite and customer prompt sets. Moving to wider rollout next week pending CI fuzz pass.
2026-02-18 Diego Ruiz: Completed 48h stress with mixed batches, no reproductions. Noted elevated op-fallback in int4 path under cold-starts; created a followup ticket ENG-57501.
2026-02-25 Sofia Nguyen (PM): Customer comms drafted; CS team to start invitations to extended canary. Ensure legal review for tenant-specific remediation notes.
2026-03-01 Observability team: Dashboard and alert live; configured QUALITY_REGRESSION_QUANT_BATCHING to include kv-fingerprint-mismatch metric.
2026-03-02 Marcus Lin: Marking several action items as started. Will update when autotuner safety gate design doc is ready.
notes: Tradeoffs considered: eager copying of prefetched blobs would eliminate aliasing but increase memory pressure and GC churn on high-throughput nodes. We prioritized fingerprint-compare + selective copy-on-write as a balanced mitigation.
Decision rationale: Fingerprint compare is cheap (8-16 byte tag) and prevents silent drift while we design a longer-term immutable cache blob approach. This allowed a fast rollback-free rollout.

Acceptance criteria for Done: (1) no kv-fingerprint-mismatch alerts for 72h under production mixed-batching traffic; (2) canary matrix includes at least 3 customers with mixed-variant workloads for 48h; (3) CI fuzz harness with coverage >= 90% on batching code paths.
